question.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\}$  of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$

current_example.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/92adebe25a1ad401ab5321664786d933e368143513a2fcb68088d263843f88eb.svg) of $\mathbb R^2,$ find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}$ if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/42dc89256befa221642155c60900057ebc55457c06e85cbd317645053a56376a.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$ 

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/8f5047a7a26eb24a1a651cbcf809bf7d0923034ca87aa4052e36f0d9501c85c9.svg) where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing the components of $\mathbf{x},$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-2-6=-8 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 3\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-4+3=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275576/assets/1f4da09e0c3737ab5566d91aec525c48be43a8716dce96dedf0821293689dcac.svg)
